name: The Sunken Barge
formed_by_story: A guild grain barge that went down at the foot of the Pilgrim Stair with its hatches open, settled into the silt on its side, and had a hollow scoured under it by forty years of lake current.
who_was_here: Eleven crew, a cargo of Hearthvale barley, and a Tallymen clerk who was counting it and did not stop.
story: The barge lies on its side on an Oroth step, half in the lake and half in a scour-hollow the current dug under it. You can walk its hull like a floor and its deck like a wall. The serpent uses the hold as a nest because the hold is the only warm place at the bottom of the Mere, and the grain is why.
unique_object: a cargo of barley still fermenting after forty years, which is what keeps the hold warm

beats.note: The Pilgrim Stair's last dry step, with the lake above it and the barge below. Light comes down green.
The scour-hollow under the hull: a tunnel the current dug, floored in silt, roofed in tarred planking.
Inside the hull, walking on what was the port side. Every fitting is ninety degrees wrong and your eye keeps arguing.
The grain hold. Warm, sour, and full of forty years of barley that has been quietly working the whole time.
The clerk's cabin, dry in an air pocket, with a tally half finished and a candle burned to the socket.
The aft hold, opened to the lake, where the current comes in and the serpent goes out.
A cargo hatch in what is now the ceiling, opening onto the Oroth step above.

shortcut.note: Shoulder it open from below and it stays open; the lake has been holding it shut for forty years and will not try again.

encounters.note: Leech-hounds in the silt, drawn by the warmth of the hold.
The crew, at their stations, on a floor that is a wall.
What the serpent leaves behind it in the aft hold: a sallowjaw grown fat on the barley, and it goes out with the current.

features.note: A tally that stops mid-column, and a column that does not add up.
